strengths: All 24 browser tests pass (node tests/run.mjs prints '24 passed, 0 failed'). They cover the filter, the URL state with back/forward, hostile query params, focus-visible outline colours, skip link, reduced motion, form validation edge cases, horizontal overflow at 360px, and blocking of any non-local request
The genre filter is a properly labelled <select> with a polite live count ('Showing 3 of 12 books'), the state is kept in the URL, and popstate/pageshow sync works

Strong accessibility: skip link, aria-current, one h1 per page, a logical h1-h2 order, and aria-invalid plus aria-describedby errors with focus moved to the first invalid field. Measured contrast: muted text 8.3:1, links 8.2:1, error 7.3:1, focus ring 6.4:1, header focus 7.6:1
Small, idiomatic, readable JS (49 and 58 lines) and a tidy CSS file with tokens. The no-JS degradation is graceful even though it isn't required
The form honestly says it is a demo and nothing was sent, with no fake success
12 books and 5 events with realistic, internally consistent copy (the mystery club picks a catalogue title, the author talk is by a catalogue author, and weekdays match dates)
README gives clear run and test instructions
reports.summary: Build W is a clean, correct and highly accessible four-page site that meets every spec requirement, with no blockers or majors. All 24 browser tests pass, covering the filter, keyboard focus, form validation and the no-external-requests rule; the only issue in the code is a minor live-region quirk. Responsive layout at 360px works in the screenshots and tests. The main weakness is the product: the visual design is very plain, with no imagery, a sparse home page and a static events list that will go stale. Every defect found is minor.

judges.verdict: All 23 builds pass over HTTP: no overflow at 360px, no external requests, and a working genre filter in each. The clearest dividing line is that A, I and J use ES-module scripts, which Chromium blocks over file://, so their catalogue and menu are empty when the files are opened directly. That cost them about a point despite strong code. Among the rest, scores separate on robustness details (events handled by date, history behaviour, errors that clear live) and content depth. The low-contrast focus ring on the checked genre pill appears in many builds (R, T, G, D, M, E), so I treated it as a shared minor issue rather than a major one for R alone.
